facts.text: Swartz began as the site of the Swartz Sawmill, owned by the E.
The 1884 arrival of the Vicksburg, Shreveport and Pacific Railroad spurred Swartz’s growth by linking farmlands to Monroe markets.
Swartz lies roughly seven miles northeast of Monroe, functioning as a suburban residential community within the Monroe metropolitan area.
Swartz hosts two elementary schools—Swartz Lower and Swartz Upper—that feed into East Ouachita Middle School and Ouachita Parish High School.
The land that became Swartz was part of the Ouachita River valley, inhabited by successive Native American cultures for thousands of years before European arrival.
Swartz’s economy today leans on health care and social assistance, construction, and retail trade, thanks to its proximity to Monroe.
